newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ACIL to sell Bass Strait oil royalty.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ACIL to sell Bass Strait oil royalty.

text.p: Australian Consolidated Investments Ltd (ACIL) said on Monday it will sell its royalty interest in the Bass Strait oil fields through a trust which will list on the Australian Stock Exchange.
ACIL said it expected to realise a profit of about A$110 million on the sale, if the offer is fully subscribed.
ACIL, formerly Bell Resources Ltd, is 96 percent owned by Brierley Investments Ltd group.

ACIL said Bass Strait Oil Management Limited, a controlled entity of ACIL which manages the trust, had issued a prospectus offering 44 million ordinary redeemable units of A$5 each in the Trust to raise A$220 million.

The consideration for the assignment of the Weeks Royalty is in two parts - the issue of 44 million ordinary units valued at A$220 million with entitlement to 10 years of royalties and 11.6 million residual units valuesd at A$174 million that are entitled to the remainder of the royalty stream.
ACIL will retain all of the residual units which will be unlisted and have a book value to ACIl of A$133 million.
The Bass Strait Royalty is a 2.5 percent overriding royalty relating to all oil and gas produced by BHP from designated areas in Bass Strait.
Under the royalty, the trust has an entitlement to receive 55.11 percent of all payments currently made by Esso and BHP, the joint venture producers in Bass Strait.
Unitholders in the trust would receive the total royalty payments made by Esso and BHP that would have been attributable to the Weeks Royalty over the 10 year term of the units.
The units would be redeemed progressively over their 10 year term through 20 equal half-yearly capital redemption payments of 25 cents each with payment guaranteed by ACIL.
Esso and BHP have paid royalties on Bass Strait production continuously since 1972.
